Work to protect DNS from quantum decryption attacks is speeding up
items.summary: Internet governance bodies are likely to accelerate work to prepare the domain name system (DNS) so it can remain secure once quantum computers can challenge conventional encryption. John Crain, ICANN’s chief technology officer, last week told The Register that he is aware of efforts within the organization, and at other internet governance bodies, to consider what happens once commercially available quantum computers become capable of easily deciphering encrypted information. Those machines theoretically pose a risk to DNSSEC, the Domain Name System Security Extensions that adapt PKI to the job of verifying the veracity of DNS records. The CTO said he’s aware of predictions that such computers could come online “at the turn of the decade” and that he has therefore changed his view of when the DNS needs to be made quantum safe. “If you asked me years ago, I would have said we probably need to be ready in ten years,” Crain said. “Now, maybe it's less than that. I don't know if it's three years or five, but it's probably not ten”. One way to quantum-proof DNSSEC is to use larger keys that even a quantum computer will struggle to crack. Doing so, however, runs into message size limits in the DNS. “If we go for larger key sizes, that means larger zones, larger packets, larger responses,” Crain said. It can also mean traffic being carried by multiple TCP packets, instead of the single UDP messages DNS prefers.

“If you asked me years ago, I would have said we probably need to be ready in ten years,” Crain said. “Now, maybe it's less than that. I don't know if it's three years or five, but it's probably not ten”.

items.title: CVE-2026-111497 Portfolio Status: Impact of Brotli Vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497) on Palo Alto Networks Products
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Workaround, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 9.2, CVEs: CVE-2026-111497, Summary: A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream. Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1. Brotli is commonly used by many HTTP-based applications including Node.js. Palo Alto Networks is actively investigating its product portfolio and cloud services to determine potential impact from this vulnerability. items.title: Technology News Nation-state  Recorded Future Ukraine warns hackers are exploiting Chinese-made Dahua surveillance cameras
items.summary: Ukrainian government cybersecurity researchers have warned that hackers are gaining unauthorized access to surveillance cameras made by Chinese manufacturer Dahua, potentially exposing video feeds and allowing attackers to remotely control the devices. Ukraine's computer emergency response team, CERT-UA, said late last week that it had identified cases in which hackers compromised the internet-connected cameras and video recorders, changed their settings and created unauthorized user accounts. The agency did not say how many devices had been compromised, when the attacks occurred or who was responsible. Chinese-made surveillance equipment remains widely used in Ukraine, including by government institutions and military units. According to CERT-UA, the attackers appear to be exploiting a feature called Easy4IP, which allows users to access Dahua cameras remotely through the manufacturer's cloud service. The feature connects devices to the cloud using their serial numbers, even when the devices are protected by firewalls or cannot be accessed directly over the internet. CERT-UA said the serial numbers follow predictable patterns, allowing hackers to guess large numbers of them and identify cameras connected to the cloud. As a result, devices with the remote access feature enabled could be vulnerable even if their serial numbers have never been publicly disclosed. Once a device is identified, attackers can attempt to gain access by guessing weak or default passwords or exploiting security flaws in outdated firmware that allow them to bypass authentication. The agency specifically warned about two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045, disclosed in 2021, that affect certain Dahua cameras and video recorders.

items.title: Honeypots Now Recording in-the-Wild PHP2Shell Exploits
items.summary: A much feared avalanche of website hacking triggered by the PHP2Shell set of vulnerabilities edged closer to reality following reports from cybersecurity researchers that honeypots are recording successful exploits. Security researchers for days have seen millions of exploit attempts, especially in the days following the PHP Foundation's hasty publication of patches after details of the flaws - tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 - leaked prematurely (see: Waiting for the PHP2Shell Onslaught as PoCs Proliferate). Adel Ka, the detection and response lead at Perplexity, reported Saturday that six of his honeypots collectively recorded 35 successful, in-the-wild exploits of PHP2Shell from two different IP addresses, which led 1.6 milliseconds later to attackers gaining root access. Malware analyst Marcus Hutchins, who's been closely tracking proof-of-concept exploits for the flaws, said "this is by far the highest quality confirmation of in-the-wild php2shell exploitation I've seen so far," and involved an Apache server running PHP 8.4.26. On Sunday, the host of the "Steal My Bitcoin CTF proof of concept" announced that a researcher successfully exploited a standard version of PHP version 8.4.26, just 19 hours after he installed it on his capture-the-flag server and invited the world to try and access the cryptocurrency wallet it contained.

items.title: Google: CVE-2026-111497 Buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 8.1, CVEs: CVE-2026-111497, Summary: Microsoft released emergency .NET security updates to patch a critical vulnerability known as Broccoli2Shell, also tracked as Node2Shell and HTTP2Shell. Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, this critical-severity flaw stems from an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder, which expands data compressed using Google's widely used Brotli lossless compression algorithm. To address this flaw, Microsoft has released out-of-band (OOB) security updates for .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10, along with .NET 11 Release Candidate 3, and advised "updating as soon as possible." Brotli decompression is not enabled by default in an out-of-the-box .NET or ASP.NET Core install. Applications must manually opt in to ASP.NET Core request decompression or HttpClient response decompression, or they must manually invoke the Brotli decompression APIs provided by .NET.

items.title: 'Gheist' Weaponizes GitHub Tokens to Steal Cloud Secrets
items.summary: An ongoing attack is abusing compromised GitHub tokens to harvest cloud secrets and credentials from thousands of developer repositories, bringing into focus how compromised developer accounts can provide a gateway into enterprise cloud environments. Dubbed "Gheist," the campaign has left more than 13,500 malicious branches — or versions of a project's code — across more than 850 compromised GitHub accounts, according to a report published over the weekend by Wiz Research.

items.title: Tuntemattomalla lähettäjätunnuksella lähetetty tekstiviesti merkitään roskapostiksi tai viestin perillepääsy estyy 2.11.2026 alkaen.
items.summary: Operaattorien on marraskuun alusta lähtien muutettava viestin lähettäjätunnus muotoon "roskaposti" tai estettävä tekstiviesti, jos viestin lähettäjällä ei ole vahvistettua käyttöoikeutta lähettäjätunnukseen, Traficom kertoo tiedotteessaan. Muutos vaikeuttaa huijareiden mahdollisuuksia esiintyä tekstiviesteissä esimerkiksi viranomaisina, yrityksinä tai muina luotettuina toimijoina. Muutos ei vaikuta yksityishenkilöiden välisiin tekstiviesteihin. – Roskaposti-merkintä kertoo vastaanottajalle, ettei lähettäjän oikeutta käyttämäänsä tunnukseen ole voitu varmistaa. Huijarin on jatkossa vaikeampi saada viesti näyttämään siltä, että se olisi tullut tutulta yritykseltä tai muulta luotetulta toimijalta, johtava asiantuntija Klaus Nieminen Traficomista kertoo.

Huijarin on jatkossa vaikeampi saada viesti näyttämään siltä, että se olisi tullut tutulta yritykseltä tai muulta luotetulta toimijalta, johtava asiantuntija Klaus Nieminen Traficomista kertoo.

items.title: PHP2Shell security flaws now sucessfully exploited in the wild
items.summary: Two critical RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), collectively tracked as PHP2Shell, have been successfully exploited in the wild. The malicious activity was caught by Adel Karimi, detection and response lead at Perplexity, whose honeypots recorded evidence of confirmed remote code execution against an Apache mod_php installation running PHP 8.4.26. "This is now confirmed RCE with usable memory disclosure, not just a crash followed by a suspicious process. The response delivered an 800 KiB decoded cookie dump, and a function address derived from that dump using the public exploit's offsets appears in the subsequent execution payload," Karimi shared.

"This is now confirmed RCE with usable memory disclosure, not just a crash followed by a suspicious process. The response delivered an 800 KiB decoded cookie dump, and a function address derived from that dump using the public exploit's offsets appears in the subsequent execution payload," Karimi shared.
